# Measure memory and page-cache pressure for N=8 session snapshots

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 4.

## Target outcome

The resource cost of holding 8 session snapshots instead of 2: per-snapshot
footprint, bytes per token, aggregate on-disk and host page-cache growth at N=8,
and the system `MemAvailable` delta — with VRAM reported as non-available rather
than guessed, per the fidelity convention in
`docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md`.

## Minimal implementation

- `--mode memory` in the harness: build N=8 distinct session prefixes, save all
  eight (bounded by free page cache), then measure:
  - on-disk size per snapshot and total (also reported by
    `du -sb` on the run's own directory);
  - `/proc/meminfo` `Cached` and `MemAvailable` before/after each save and after
    the full set, plus the page-cache residency of the snapshot files;
  - read-back bandwidth: sequential read of each snapshot to `/dev/null` (the
    proxy's restore path reads the whole file), giving MiB/s — the term that
    determines restore cost as snapshots grow.
- Derive bytes/token per size and extrapolate to N=8 for a realistic mix,
  stating the mix used.
- Record the ROCm VRAM reading and mark it explicitly non-available/ungraded
  (the known-degraded ~0.2 GB reading), instead of reporting a false number.
- Emit `results/<label>/memory.json` + markdown table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-size snapshot footprint and bytes/token, measured (not derived-only).
- N=8 aggregate footprint (sum of snapshot sizes) and observed `Cached` growth,
  with the delta between them explained (page cache vs. written-but-not-resident).
- `MemAvailable` delta across a full N=8 set, and the maximum resident footprint
  observed during the run.
- Read-back bandwidth (MiB/s) for snapshot files, which the verdict uses to
  extrapolate restore cost.
- VRAM is either measured credibly or explicitly reported as non-available with
  the reason; no estimated VRAM figure is presented as measured.
- The run cleans up the snapshots it created and reports the post-cleanup
  `MemAvailable` / `Cached` return-to-baseline.

## Constraints

- Must not fill the page cache to the point of harming live inference: the run
  is bounded by a `--max-write-mib` guard (default sized from current
  `MemAvailable`) and stops early, recording truncation.
- No `drop_caches` unless explicitly permitted by the operator; measure the
  natural page-cache behaviour instead.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/kv_memory_table.py` (per-token KV expectation reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/memory.json` (new artifact)
- `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`

# Results doc: tables, break-even model, go/no-go verdict and substitutes

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Satisfies AC2, AC3, AC4 and AC5 of the spike.

## Target outcome

A committed document `docs/virtual-slot-spike-LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE.md` containing
the complete measured tables, an explicit break-even inequality, a go/no-go
verdict, and — if not viable — the cheaper substitutes ranked with the measured
evidence for each.

## Minimal implementation

- Assemble the tables from the four measurement children's JSON artifacts
  (save size/time, restore time, restore hit-rate, invalidated-restore rate,
  memory delta, contention A/B). Cross-link each number to its result file and
  commit so the doc is auditable, not just descriptive.
- Break-even model, stated as an inequality with every term measured:
  `hit_rate × (cold_prefill_s − restore_s) > (1 − hit_rate) × eviction_reprefill_s + save_s_share`
  — or an equivalent explicit form — with the measured values substituted and
  the resulting break-even `hit_rate*` solved for each prompt size. State the
  cold-prefill baseline used (window median 61.8 s dispatch-first-byte, p90
  269.8 s) and the solitary cold-prefill figures from the parent's impact
  analysis (~254 new tok/s).
- Verdict: `go` (build virtual slots) / `no-go` (not viable) / `conditional`
  (viable only under a named condition), each with the driving measurement
  quoted. If `no-go`, rank the substitutes with measured evidence:
  more physical slots (LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8 — keep N=2 pending
  LP-0MVGPEP3O000RKKD), idle-aware admission (LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J implementation
  done; LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD / LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF measurement), shorter
  post-stream lease (locate and cite the owning item).
- Fidelity section reproducing the caveat conventions
  (`docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md`): what could not be measured,
  VRAM non-availability, and the live-load validity caveat if applicable.
- AC5 proof: a `No production behaviour change` section listing the commits
  touched (`git diff --stat` restricted to `proxy/benchmarks/`, `proxy/tests/`,
  `docs/`), confirming `proxy/config.yaml` sha unchanged and proxy healthy after
  the runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/virtual-slot-spike-LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE.md` committed with all six
  required tables: save size/time, restore time, restore hit-rate,
  invalidated-restore rate, memory delta, end-to-end contention metrics.
- The break-even condition is an explicit inequality with measured terms
  substituted, and the break-even hit-rate is solved per prompt size.
- Verdict is one of `go` / `no-go` / `conditional`, with the decisive measurement
  quoted and linked to its result artifact.
- If `no-go` or `conditional`, at least three cheaper substitutes are named with
  the measured evidence for each (or, where a substitute is unmeasured, that is
  stated as an open measurement with the owning work-item id).
- A fidelity/caveats section states every non-measured quantity explicitly, with
  no estimated value presented as measured.
- AC5 is evidenced: the diff touches only benchmark/test/doc paths, config sha
  unchanged, proxy verified healthy after the runs.
- Every number in the doc traces to a committed result file.

## Constraints

- Read-only on production configuration. No items in `proxy/proxy/` modified.
- The doc must not re-derive historical baselines it can cite (61.8 s median,
  269.8 s p90 from the parent's window).

## Key Files

- `docs/virtual-slot-spike-LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE.md` (new)
- `docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md` (format/caveat reference)
- `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` (validity-caveat reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/*.json`

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the parent item's gating precondition verified from
measured evidence, so that prefill tuning only starts once local actually
carries sustained work.

## What the gate is

Parent **LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT** AC0 requires a comment recording a measured
**>60 % local (GPU) busy** night before any change is made. Busy is the
`## Local model utilization` upper bound (dispatch -> finish: prefill +
decode) from the deterministic `proxy-usage-analysis` CLI, over a complete
night window (22:00-07:00 local).

## Evidence at planning time (2026-10-25)

- Night **2026-10-23 22:00 -> 2026-10-24 07:00**: busy **2.2 %** (719 s of
  32 400 s; 27 local streams; prefill 336 slot-s; decode 383 slot-s;
  idle 97.8 %).
  Command:
  `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "2026-10-23 22:00:00" --end "2026-10-24 07:00:00" --output-dir /tmp/wl-gate-check --json`
- Same night in the 24 h daily report (`~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`,
  window 2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52): busy 10.2 %.

**The gate is NOT met.** The parent is left `blocked` at stage
`plan_complete`, and every other child of this plan depends on this item, so
none of them is dispatchable until the gate passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0: The gate AC is satisfied - a comment on this item records the measured >60% GPU utilisation for a full night, from the usage-analysis report, before any change is made.
- AC1: A comment on the parent records local busy % for a **complete** night
  window (22:00-07:00), with the exact CLI invocation, the window bounds and
  the artifact directory used.
- AC2: The gate is declared met **only** when `busy_pct >= 60` for the whole
  night (`definition: dispatch_to_finish` in the CLI `--json` summary).
- AC3: When the gate is not met this item stays **open and incomplete** with
  the evidence comment (recorded `blocked` status is derived from dependency
  edges in `wl` and cannot be pinned, so this item is the lock: keeping it
  incomplete keeps every dependent child dependency-blocked), and no other
  child of the plan is started.
- AC6: This item must never be marked `completed` while the gate is unmet. If a
  run cannot leave it open, it records the evidence and files the deferral on
  the parent rather than completing the gate.
- AC4: When the gate is met this item completes with the evidence comment and
  the parent plus its dependent siblings are unblocked in the same update
  sequence.
- AC5: Measurement only - no configuration, flag or code change.

**Key Files:**
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` - deterministic report CLI
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` - report section definitions

## Dependencies

None. All other children of this plan depend on this item.

## Problem

`X-Local-Preference: local-only` is enforced in **exactly two** places — the admission decisions at `provider.py:6753` (contention-queue path, `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot`) and `provider.py:11027` (direct/lease path, inside `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`). Every other reason the local entry is dropped from the chain simply `continue`s to the next provider, so a client that pinned its work to the local GPU can be served by a paid remote provider **without any signal** to the client or the log.

`_request_local_preference()` call sites (`grep` over `proxy/proxy/provider.py`):

```
6305 def _request_local_preference(...)
6753   ← enforced (queue admission, _maybe_queue_for_local_slot)
9517   ← log only (priority_routing, _proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle)
11027  ← enforced (direct admission, _proxy_with_fallback_cycle)
```

Skip paths that ignore it (all end in `continue` → next provider):

| Path | Log line | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Local entry in cooldown | `Skipping provider=local-qwen3: local-qwen3 in cooldown (675s remaining)` | `provider.py:7160` |
| Router skip (context too large, resident prefix insufficient, prefill thrash cooldown, economic/idle bypass) | `routing_skip_local … reason=… → skipping local, routing to next remote provider` | `provider.py:10739`, `:10271` |
| Contention-queue caps exceeded / queue expiry | `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue … queued_duration=…` | `provider.py:10355`, `:11358` |
| Prefill gate / lease denied (actions other than `refused_local_only`) | `local_dispatch_denied …`, `prefill_gate_wait_ms=…` | lease/gate branches |
| Local entry context cap (`max_context_tokens`) / quota hard stop | `routing_skip_provider_context …`, `Skipping provider=…: <quota stop reason>` | `provider.py:3325`, `:7160` |

Note the asymmetry: the opposite intent (`remote-ok`) *is* enforced structurally — `apply_local_preference()` strips local entries from the chain (`proxy/proxy/priority.py:410`) — so only `local-only` can leak.

## Evidence (2026-10-25)

Session `herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152` sent `X-Local-Preference: local-only` (confirmed on its 11:46–11:57 requests) and was nonetheless served by **OpenCode Go** at 11:32:47, 11:33:35 and 11:34:48 while its local route was contended/skipped (`contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`, `routing_resident_prefix … decision=resident_prefix_insufficient`). It is not possible to prove the header was on those three requests because request headers are never logged, and `priority_routing … preference=` carries no session id — hence AC5 below.

## Goal

A `local-only` request either completes locally or receives the local-only refusal — it is never silently served by a remote provider, and any deviation is attributable from the log.

## Users

- **herdr worker sessions** that pin `X-Local-Preference: local-only` to keep paid-remote costs at zero (e.g. the 2026-10-25 session `herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152`). With this defect, they are billed for remote serve without consent.
  - As a local-only client, I want every local-skip reason to end in the refusal (`429` + `X-Local-Route: refused`), so the proxy never silently spends my remote budget.
- **Proxy operators** reading `proxy.log`.
  - As an operator, I want each skip/fallback decision to log the parsed preference, so a local-only violation is attributable to a session without header-correlation heuristics.

## Acceptance criteria

1. With `X-Local-Preference: local-only`, **no** remote provider is dispatched for any skip reason: cooldown, router skip (`context_too_large`, `resident_prefix_insufficient`, `prefill_thrash_cooldown`, economic/idle bypass), contention-queue cap/expiry, prefill-gate or lease denial, entry context cap, quota hard stop.
2. Each of those outcomes returns the local-only refusal response (429, `X-Local-Route: refused`, `X-Local-Fallback-Reason: <skip reason>`) rather than falling through; the reason the local route was unavailable is carried in the body/headers.
3. `prefer-local` (default) behaviour is unchanged for every one of those paths — it still falls through to the next provider exactly as today.
4. Every skip/fallback line that decides "not local" logs the parsed preference (`preference=local-only|prefer-local|remote-ok`) so an intent violation is visible in `proxy.log`; `priority_routing` keeps its existing fields (additive change only).
5. Attribution is possible: the `priority_routing …` line (or its successor) carries the session id / request id, so a preference can be tied to a specific request without correlation heuristics.
6. Tests: one test per skip reason asserting local-only ⇒ refusal and prefer-local ⇒ remote dispatch (table-driven); a regression test asserting `remote-ok` still strips local; a test asserting the preference appears on the skip/fallback log line.
7. `proxy/docs/routing.md` states that `local-only` is enforced on every exit from the local route, not only at the admission guard.

## Constraints

- `prefer-local` (the default for every client that does not send the header) must remain byte-compatible with today's fall-through behaviour on all paths.
- The refusal response shape must match the sibling item LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ (same 429 / `X-Local-Route: refused` / headers / body contract) so clients discriminate on one stable shape; see that item's `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`provider.py:6310`).
- No new config knobs required unless a skip reason genuinely cannot wait: prefer-local-only refusals to carry the existing refusal headers.
- `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` must carry a stable per-reason token (matching log `reason=` values) so clients can classify without parsing prose.

## Existing state

- `local-only` enforced only at the two admission decisions (`provider.py:6753`, `:11027`); every other skip `continue`s to remote.
- `remote-ok` enforced structurally by `apply_local_preference()` (`priority.py:410`); chain-emptied case falls through to the exhaustion path unchanged.
- Refusal builders already exist and are tested: `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`provider.py:6310`) on the contention-queue paths; the direct-lease path currently funnels through `_build_exhausted_response()` → `_local_admission_reject_payload()` (see LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ — the two paths disagree on `error` text).

## Desired change

- Introduce a single local-only refusal choke point (or reuse `_build_local_only_refusal_response`) so every `continue` that would otherwise leave the local route short-circuits to the refusal when `_request_local_preference(request) == "local-only"`.
- Log `preference=<parsed>` on each skip/fallback line (additive to existing fields) and thread the session/request id into `priority_routing`.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_request_local_preference()` (`:6305`), enforcement points (`:6753`, `:11027`), skip paths (`:7160`, `:10271`, `:10355`, `:10739`, `:11358`), refusal builders (`:6310`, `:5521`), `_note_local_fallback_reason()` (`:6286`), `_stamp_local_route_headers()` (`:6387`).
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — `apply_local_preference()` (`:410`), `local_preference_for_request()` (`:398`) — structural `remote-ok` filter, the model for making `local-only` structural too.
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — `parse_preference()` (`:415`), the canonical header parser (`local-only`/`prefer-local`/`remote-ok`, unknown → `prefer-local`).
- `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py`, `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — existing refusal-path tests; table-driven per-skip-reason tests are added here.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — `X-Local-Preference` semantics (`:1158`), `X-Local-Route` values (`:1173`); AC7 doc update lands here.

## Related work

- LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ (parent) — same-shape refusal contract; this item extends enforcement from the two guard sites to every skip path.
- LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL — introduced `X-Local-Preference` + AC4 refusal mechanics (completed).
- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA admission guard (completed).
- LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7 — cold-prefill budget enforcement (completed).
- LP-0MVI63OM1009K51W — lease-owner retention grace (blocked).

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: the two refusal paths converge on the LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ shape *before* or *with* this item; if that parent lands first, this item reuses its builder.
- Risk: turning every skip into a refusal changes latency/UX for legitimate local-only requests (they will now 429 instead of silently completing remotely). # Feature: preference vocabulary — add `local-preferred`, alias `local-only`

Parent: LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY. Depends-on: none. Depended-on-by: LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ, LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE, LP-0MVSHXTX1007D58Z.

## Problem statement

The proxy's `X-Local-Preference` vocabulary is defined three times over — a
canonical table in `admission_reserve.py` plus hand-rolled copies in
`priority.py` and `provider.py` — and its only "pin local" value is the
absolute `local-only`. The parent epic replaces `local-only` with
`local-preferred` (defer while local-capable, remote once the prompt outgrows
local capacity), but every downstream behaviour change is unimplementable
until the wire vocabulary itself is widened and the alias accepted. Without
this item, changing the vocabulary would silently break deployed herdr
workers that still send `local-only`, and the three parsers would keep
drifting apart.

## Users

- As a **proxy maintainer**, I want one canonical definition of the preference
  vocabulary so a new value is added in exactly one place and both routing
  cycles agree by construction.
- As a **deployed herdr worker** still sending `X-Local-Preference: local-only`,
  I want my existing header accepted and normalised, so upgrading the proxy does
  not break my dispatches.
- As a **sibling-item implementer** (LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ / LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE),
  I want `local-preferred` to already parse to a stable constant, so the
  deferral semantics land on top of the vocabulary instead of re-inventing it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** `admission_reserve.parse_preference({"x-local-preference": "local-preferred"}) == "local-preferred"`, and `parse_preference({"x-local-preference": "local-only"}) == "local-preferred"` (alias normalised).
- **AC2** Sending the legacy alias emits exactly one deprecation log line per request (level `WARNING`, naming both `local-only` and `local-preferred`), not one per skip/refusal line within that request.
- **AC3** Header lookup stays case-insensitive (`Local-Only`, `LOCAL-PREFERRED` both accepted) and unknown values / absent header keep falling back to `prefer-local` with no behaviour change versus today (LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL AC8).
- **AC4** Exactly one preference parser and one set of preference constants exist in the codebase: `priority.py` and `provider.py` import them from `admission_reserve.py`; no second `VALID_PREFERENCES` tuple, no second local `"local-only"` / `"remote-ok"` literal used for a routing comparison.
- **AC5** Behaviour is unchanged at every comparison site: after normalisation, `local-only` and `local-preferred` clients are still treated as *pin-local* by the existing choke points and refusal builders (terminal 429, never a silent fall-through). Deferral semantics remain out of scope here.
- **AC6** Tests cover the four vocabulary cases — `local-preferred` parses, mixed-case alias normalises, unknown value → `prefer-local`, absent header → `prefer-local` — plus the once-per-request deprecation, and pass under the changed-scope gate (`/skill:test --scope changed`).
- **AC7** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, docstrings, the `proxy/docs/routing.md` `X-Local-Preference` table (new canonical value + legacy-alias note) and the `proxy/config.yaml` preference commentary.
- **AC8** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No semantic change in this item.** The verdict split (deferrable vs
  too-large-for-local), the deferral path and the retryable-429 timing belong
  to LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ and LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE. This item must leave every
  routing outcome byte-identical for all four wire values.
- **Wire compatibility is mandatory.** `local-only` must never become an
  unknown value: that would demote deployed clients to `prefer-local` and let
  their requests go remote behind their back — a contract violation of
  LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL AC4 and of LP-0MVRMC1L3006F0F3's choke point.
- **One source of truth.** The alias must be expressed as a constant, not as
  string literals sprinkled at call sites; AC4 is enforced by review and by the
  "no second literal" test.
- **No client-side work.** herdr `LocalPreference` plumbing and Worklog header
  injection are out of scope (owned by the ContextHub store).
- **Documentation boundary.** `proxy/docs/routing.md` gains only the vocabulary
  row and the wire-compat note; the full `local-preferred` semantics prose is
  LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57's deliverable, so this item must not pre-empt it.
- **Scope creep guard.** Any further opportunity discovered while implementing
  (e.g. a stale `local_only` token in observability, a metrics label) is
  recorded as a new linked work item rather than absorbed here.

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py:56-63` — `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY`, `PREF_PREFER_LOCAL`, `PREF_REMOTE_OK`, `VALID_PREFERENCES`, `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE`, `HEADER_PREFERENCE`. `parse_preference()` at :468 does lower-case lookup on `x-local-preference` / `X-Local-Preference`, returns `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE` for missing/unknown, and logs `logger.debug` for unknown values.
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py:388-407` — `local_preference_for_request()` re-imports `parse_preference`, caches on `request._local_preference`, and hard-codes `"prefer-local"` as its exception fallback. `apply_local_preference()` at :409 compares the raw literal `"remote-ok"`.

# Feature: capacity verdict — deferrable vs too-large-for-local

Parent: LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY.

## Goal

One authoritative classification of *why* the local route cannot serve a request right now, so chain selection can distinguish "wait, a slot is coming" from "this prompt will never fit local".

## Deliverables

- A single verdict helper (e.g. `local_capacity_verdict(...)`) in the admission/reserve module, consumed by both dispatch cycles and the refusal builder — derived from the existing estimator/guard decision and the local provider's configured limits, **not** a second ETA or token-estimation implementation.
- Verdict vocabulary:
  - `deferrable` — prompt is inside the local serving envelope; the blocking reason is temporal (`eta_exceeds_budget_direct`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline`, queue/occupancy, lease denial, busy slots, stall/cooldown).
  - `too_large` — prompt exceeds the local serving envelope: context above the local model's limit/`cold_threshold` verdict, or `new_tokens > local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` (`prefill_budget_exceeded`).
- The verdict (and the underlying reason token) appears in the 429 payload and in a dedicated log line, so a deferral is never mistaken for chain exhaustion (relates to LP-0MVNTJQVB007QWEZ and LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ).
- Unit tests for the classification table.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 `deferrable` is returned for the observed incident shape (`eta_prefill_s=31.7`, `projected_wait_s=63.4`, `budget_s=60.0`, `new_tokens=6627`, `budget_tokens=25000`).
- AC2 `too_large` is returned when `new_tokens > local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens`, and when the local context check already skips the local route for size.
- AC3 Exactly one implementation is used by both dispatch cycles and the refusal builder (assert by import/call-site review, not by duplicated logic).
- AC4 The verdict is observable: refusal body carries it and one log line states preference + verdict + reason.
- AC5 Table-driven unit tests cover deferrable, too-large (both triggers) and non-guard temporal reasons.
- AC6 All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and docstrings; operator-facing docs (`docs/`, `proxy/config.yaml` commentary) are tracked in LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57.
- AC7 Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes

Do not pre-empt the retry-timing contract (LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X) — this item only classifies; timing stays in `_refusal_retry_timing`.

Classification inputs come from the existing estimator/guard decision and the configured envelope (`local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens`, local context limit); no second ETA, token-estimation or sizing model is introduced (parent assumption A1).

## Constraints

- One helper, imported by both dispatch cycles and the refusal builder — a duplicated verdict in `provider.py` violates AC3.
- Verdict values are exactly `deferrable` and `too_large`; an unclassifiable case must default to the existing pin-local refusal (fail safe: never promote a fits-local request to remote).
- No retry-timing change, no queue or lease behaviour change, no config default change.
- `prefer-local` and `remote-ok` behaviour is untouched by the verdict.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — the single `local_capacity_verdict(...)` helper, the `deferrable` / `too_large` vocabulary, and placement beside the existing canonical reason-token table.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `evaluate_admission()`, `suggested_retry_after_seconds()` and `COLD_PREFILL_BUDGET_KEY` supply the verdict inputs (no duplicate estimator).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — both dispatch cycles plus the refusal builder call the helper; the verdict appears in the 429 body and in one log line.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` and the local model's context limit define the serving envelope (read-only here; commentary is LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — table-driven tests covering deferrable, both too-large triggers and non-guard temporal reasons.
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` — helper-level classification unit tests.
